_comment: P3-E E5 — the ONE authority of published-contract maturity.
This is contractual policy, not roadmap state and not an operational status. It answers
exactly one question per published module: may its public ABI change, and under what
conditions. It is deliberately NOT DSL_SURFACE_MANIFEST: that manifest classifies
constructors in the pipeline authoring surface, and this classifies the artifacts an
external CONSUMER compiles against. Reusing it would conflate a DSL function with a
library ABI and quietly make the stricter policy apply to the wrong surface.
Taxonomy (the canonical one; nothing outside it is accepted):
STABLE                 breaking is forbidden except across an explicit major boundary
PARTIAL                additive changes allowed; breaking needs a recorded exception
EXPERIMENTAL           breaking allowed under a recorded decision with a stated boundary
DEPRECATED             members may be removed only after the declared removal boundary
UNSUPPORTED_FAIL_CLOSED the construct refuses itself; there is no compatibility surface
Consumed by P3EPublishedContractMaturityFitnessTest, which fails the build when a module
published from build.gradle.kts has no entry here. See publishedContractExceptions() in
the same test for how a deliberate breaking change is recorded rather than discussed.

pipeline-domain: EXPERIMENTAL, and the reason is specific rather than convenient: this module is the
innermost seam and its types are re-exported through pipeline-events and
pipeline-scripting-api, so almost every change to it is additive-by-necessity rather
than by choice. The one class of change this repository made repeatedly in P3-E is
enriching an internal decision ADT with evidence the producer already had
(WaitUntilReconciliationDecision.Aborted gained the attempt it had been discarding into
a string). That is a real breaking change to a published data class, and pretending
otherwise would make the classification a description of what we wish were true.
Promoting it to STABLE requires that the decision ADTs stop being part of the external
surface — i.e. that consumers resolve outcomes through event projections rather than
reaching for domain ADTs directly. That is S5.4's work, and until it lands the honest
pipeline-scripting-api: EXPERIMENTAL: the DSL is the authored authoring surface and several of its constructs
are already deprecated with a declared replacement (catchError, LFC1-007), which is the
signature of a surface still converging.
pipeline-events: EXPERIMENTAL: the wire vocabulary is published and load-bearing, and this block is
actively changing it (typed projections, fail-closed decoders). It is not a frozen
contract yet, and calling it one would only defer the work.
pipeline-output: EXPERIMENTAL: the smallest of the four and the least consumed; nothing in the P3-E
